# Spatial outputs {#sec-maps}

To translate the tabular synthesis from @sec-synthesis into spatially explicit maps of IUCN GET Ecosystem Functional Groups across Tasmania, we join our synthesised membership tables to the polygon attribute table of TASVEG 5.0 (`TASVEG_5_0.shp`) and export either raster GeoTIFFs or vector GeoPackages.

::: {.callout-important}
## Separation of analytical documentation and heavy spatial output generation
Full-state 90 m rasterisation (`fasterize`) and multi-layer GeoTIFF stack operations take ~2 minutes per run and write large geospatial files. Those production steps are therefore **kept in separate standalone scripts** (`scripts/TASVEG-xref-IUCNGET-output-best-90m.R`, `scripts/EFG-membership-raster.R`, `scripts/TASVEG-membership-matrices.R`, and `scripts/EFG-membership-vector.R`; documented in @sec-outputs). In this chapter, heavy rasterisation and multi-layer `terra::app()` chunks are shown with `eval: false` for transparency, while pre-generated GeoTIFF outputs from `results/best-candidate/` are loaded directly for a fast visual preview.
:::

:::{.aside}
Our setup for this R session loads raster/vector libraries (`terra`, `sf`, `fasterize`), `dplyr`, `readr`, `ecoSynthesis`, and `geco` (for standard Global Ecosystems Atlas pixel codes and hex colour palettes), and loads the validated membership table:

```{r}
#| eval: true
#| code-fold: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| code-summary: Setup for this R session
library(terra)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(ecoSynthesis)
library(geco)
library(fasterize)

here::i_am("synthesis/EFG-map.qmd")
output_dir <- here::here("../results/XREFs")
best_dir <- here::here("../results/best-candidate")
load(here::here(output_dir, "memb-tables.rda"))

efg_pixel_values <- geco_efg_data() |>
    select(efg_code, efg_pixel_value) |>
    rename("EFG" = "efg_code")
```

:::

## Joining synthesis tables to TASVEG 5.0 polygons

The TASVEG 5.0 statewide shapefile contains hundreds of thousands of polygons, each carrying a `VEGCODE` attribute. We inspect its non-spatial attribute table first via `sf::read_sf()` and `sf::st_drop_geometry()`:

```{r}
TASVEG_xy <- read_sf(here::here("..", "gisdata", "LIST_TASVEG_50_STATEWIDE", "TASVEG_5_0.shp"))

TASVEG_xy |>
    st_drop_geometry()
```

The synthesis strategy chosen in @sec-synthesis directly determines the structure of the spatial output:

- **Best-candidate ("winner-takes-all") synthesis** (`keep_all = FALSE`) creates a strict **many-to-one** join to polygons, allowing the entire state to be represented by three compact 90 m raster layers (best-candidate EFG pixel code, `prop_memb`, and `supporting` interpreter count; Output 3 in @sec-outputs).
- **All-candidates synthesis** (`keep_all = TRUE`) creates a **many-to-many** relationship, requiring either one raster layer per candidate EFG (31 GeoTIFFs; Output 2) or a polygon vector GeoPackage for a selected EFG or bundled interpreter matrices (Output 1 and Derived Outputs in @sec-outputs).

## Best-candidate synthesis join

Here we aggregate Round 2 assessments to a single best-candidate EFG per `VEGCODE` via `ecoSynthesis::summarise_membership(keep_all = FALSE, which_round = 2)`:

```{r}
TASVEG_best_summary <-
    summarise_membership(TASVEG_clean, keep_all = FALSE, which_round = 2)
```

Next, we join `TASVEG_best_summary` onto `TASVEG_xy` (`many-to-one` on `VEGCODE`) and attach the standard Global Ecosystems Atlas integer pixel codes (`efg_pixel_value`) from `geco::geco_efg_data()`:

```{r}
TASVEG_xy_best <- TASVEG_xy |>
    left_join(TASVEG_best_summary, by = "VEGCODE", relationship = "many-to-one") |>
    left_join(efg_pixel_values, by = "EFG")
```

We verify that the polygon count is unchanged (no accidental row duplication during the join) and inspect a random sample of 10 joined polygon attributes:

```{r}
nrow(TASVEG_xy_best) == nrow(TASVEG_xy)

set.seed(42)
TASVEG_xy_best |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    select(VEG_GROUP, VEGCODE, EFG, prop_memb, supporting, efg_pixel_value) |>
    slice_sample(n = 10)
```

## Rasterisation workflow (illustrative; executed separately)

The code block below illustrates how the standalone script `scripts/TASVEG-xref-IUCNGET-output-best-90m.R` rasterises `TASVEG_xy_best` onto a 90 m × 90 m grid (`EPSG:28355`) using `fasterize::fasterize()`—chosen over `terra::rasterize()` based on the speed benchmarks in @sec-reproducibility—attaches the official Global Ecosystems Atlas colour table (`coltab()`) and GDAL metadata tags (`metags()`), and writes the GeoTIFFs. It is marked `eval: false` so it is not re-executed during book rendering:

```{r}
#| eval: false
rez <- 90
TASVEG_raster <- raster::raster(TASVEG_xy, res = rez)

# Rasterise best-candidate membership proportion, EFG pixel code, and support count
memb_raster <- fasterize(
    TASVEG_xy_best,
    TASVEG_raster,
    field = "prop_memb",
    fun = "max"
) |> rast()

target_raster <- fasterize(
    TASVEG_xy_best,
    TASVEG_raster,
    field = "efg_pixel_value",
    fun = "first"
) |> rast()

supp_raster <- fasterize(
    TASVEG_xy_best,
    TASVEG_raster,
    field = "supporting",
    fun = "max"
) |> rast()

# Embed Global Ecosystems Atlas colour table and GDAL metadata tags
ctab <- geco_efg_data() |> transmute(value = efg_pixel_value, color = efg_hex_code)
coltab(target_raster) <- ctab

rast_metadata <- c(
    PROJECT = "Ecosystem Indicators Workflows",
    TITLE = "Best candidate ecosystem functional group",
    DESCRIPTION = "Synthesis of crossreference from TASVEG 5.0 to IUCN GET"
)
metags(target_raster) <- rast_metadata

writeRaster(
    target_raster,
    here::here(best_dir, "TASVEG-xref-target.tiff"),
    overwrite = TRUE
)
```

## Preview of pre-generated 90 m best-candidate GeoTIFFs

Rather than repeating the rasterisation step, the lightweight chunk below loads the pre-generated GeoTIFFs from `results/best-candidate/` (published on Zenodo as @OUTPUT1_best_candidate; see @sec-outputs) and displays the best-candidate EFG map alongside its spatial certainty layer (`prop_memb`):

```{r}
#| eval: true
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6
target_tif <- here::here(best_dir, "TASVEG-xref-target.tiff")
memb_tif <- here::here(best_dir, "TASVEG-xref-membership.tiff")
lut_csv <- here::here(best_dir, "IUCN-GET-pixel-lookup.csv")

if (file.exists(target_tif) && file.exists(memb_tif)) {
    r_target <- rast(target_tif)
    r_memb <- rast(memb_tif)

    if (file.exists(lut_csv)) {
        efg_lut <- read_csv(lut_csv, show_col_types = FALSE)
        levels(r_target) <- data.frame(
            id = efg_lut$efg_pixel_value,
            EFG = efg_lut$EFG
        )
    }

    old_par <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(3, 3, 3, 4))
    plot(r_target, main = "Best-candidate IUCN GET EFG (90 m)")
    plot(r_memb, main = "Membership proportion (prop_memb)")
    par(old_par)
} else {
    message("Pre-generated GeoTIFFs not found in results/best-candidate/; run scripts/TASVEG-xref-IUCNGET-output-best-90m.R first.")
}
```

## Multi-layer EFG membership raster stacks (illustrative)

When all 31 candidate EFGs are rasterised separately into individual 90 m membership layers (`scripts/EFG-membership-raster.R` → `results/efg-membership-rasters/`; Output 2 in @sec-outputs), the full stack can be read into `terra` to cross-check the dominant layer index (`which.max`) and maximum membership (`max`) per pixel across all layers. Because pixel-wise `terra::app()` over 31 statewide 90 m rasters is computationally slow, these diagnostic commands are shown with `eval: false`:

```{r}
#| eval: false
efg_rast_dir <- here::here("../results/efg-membership-rasters")
tas_all <- rast(dir(efg_rast_dir, pattern = "-memb-90m\\.tiff$", full.names = TRUE))

# Identify which EFG layer achieves the highest prop_memb at each 90 m pixel
tas_which <- app(tas_all, fun = "which.max", na.rm = TRUE)
plot(tas_which, main = "Layer index of maximum EFG membership")

# Compute the maximum prop_memb value across all 31 candidate EFG layers
tas_max <- app(tas_all, fun = "max", na.rm = TRUE)
plot(tas_max, main = "Maximum EFG membership across all 31 layers")
```
